title: PR6030's local P104 word has no chart-only headroom in five edit classes (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**No chart-only edit in five searched classes improves the paid moment of the selected PR6030 local P104 word.** The same holds for the PR5907 and PR5827 words. No new κ. Card `selected-packing` (incumbent optimization), scope refined to the exact PR6030 word.

Package: `research/p104-chart-assignment-rigidity/` (base `721c03822`).

## Why this question

PR6030's fixed invoice is already packed to its root: the review encloses the raw crossing in (0.00312581155791, 0.00312581155792). A packing step therefore needs a changed paid profile. In PR5827's `local.py`, a MOVE `a -> b` is a paid call of rank `|dim b - dim a|`, and a helper's credit is `dim(final) - dim(initial)`. Scalar events need a common chart but any common chart will do. So the paid profile has one degree of freedom that does not touch the scalar program: which frame each register occupies, and when. Merging two moves of ranks `x, y` gains `x^t + y^t - (x+y)^t` per LOCAL call at unchanged targets. That is about `1.39·C` for 1+1 and `2.25·C` for PR6030's own 1+3, so any such merge would be a hill-climbing step.

## Classes searched (PR6030 word)

| Class | Edit | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A. rung skip by retiming | Delete one stay `a -> b -> c`. Each of its events, SCALEs included, commutes to a slot where its partner is at `a` or `c`. | 2,664 stays; none admits a retiming |
| B. listed-frame re-chart | Move a whole meeting (stays joined by scalar events) to any of the 1,093 listed frames that nest. Optionally helper endpoints move too. | 41 legal (19,312 with helper endpoints); none gains |
| C. any-subspace re-chart | As B, over every dimension between the span of the lower neighbours and the intersection of the upper ones. Exact per meeting, since cost depends only on dimension. | 743 free meetings (834); 87 (163) have slack; none gains |
| D. split skip | Delete a stay and re-chart partner sub-meetings to `a` (before a threshold) or `c` (after). | 80 legal thresholds, all losing |
| E. joint pair re-chart | Two meetings linked by a MOVE, re-charted together to listed frames. | 1,238 pairs, 209 legal; none gains |

PR5907's and PR6030's frame-593 rung removals lie outside these classes. PR6030's README says its edit also rewrote the ordinary ADD/SCALE events (ADD 21,706 -> 18,404) and rerouted reads through other helpers. The practical message for climbers: the simple chart moves are exhausted on this word, so start from a scalar-program change (read rerouting) and then re-chart.

## Evidence

`python3.12 -I -B research/p104-chart-assignment-rigidity/verify.py` uses only the stdlib and takes under 90 s. It imports PR5827's `local.py` unchanged. `scripts/research_package.py --package ...` reports `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, and `RESULT.json` regenerates byte for byte.

- Class A proposals and positive class B proposals are replayed by `local.py`, which checks all public and owned rows, strict nesting, ownership and frame tags. C, D and E are priced by the nesting rule with the per-LOCAL proxy `t = 1 - 0.0031258`. None of them is positive on the real words.
- **Controls on the PR6030 word:**
  1. an inserted unread rung (register 76, frames 3 -> 81 -> 252) is found by A-D, with gain `2 - 2^t`;
  2. a worsened meeting chart (meeting 2620, frame 1057 -> 782) is found by B, C and E;
  3. the rung from (1) holding two `SCALE -1` events is found by A, which must relocate both, and by B.

  All three perturbed words pass the replay first.
- A read-only OpenAI Codex adversarial review raised three points, all addressed in the second commit. (1) In class A, SCALEs stayed in place and blocked ADD retiming; they are now relocated and the stay's own events are not barriers. (2) The headline overclaimed; it is now scoped to the classes. (3) The docstring overstated replay coverage. The review confirmed that class C's dimension argument is correct under `local.py`'s strict nesting, with equal-frame edges deleted as rank-0 merges. This is AI review only. Hosted CI was not monitored.

## Not covered and open next questions

- This is a finite search, not an optimality proof. Class C is coordinate-wise, and class E covers pairs over listed frames only. Re-charting three or more linked meetings, or a pair over arbitrary subspaces, is open.
- Class A has no control in which an ADD partner must be met at a different slot.
- Native maps for new frame pairs, the compiler, the caller and the outer rows are not exercised, because no proposal reached them.
- **Read rerouting, then re-chart:** can reads like PR6030's (helper 268 reads `2·704` at frame 714, and helper 560 no longer reads 704 at frame 612) be enumerated from the `local.py` row replay, and does each rewritten word then open a class A-E move?

All five inherited framework assumptions and the selected record are unchanged. No merge or frontier change is requested.

## Credit

The words are DreamingOfClouds' (PR6030, PR5907) and Ali Romman's (PR5827, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance). They rest on PR5811 (Mason Hale) and the lineage back to PR5565 (Pierre-Loic Doulcet). The replay checker is PR5827's `local.py`. This PR adds only the census and controls.
